meaning:
παρά-βασις, -εως, ἡ
(παραβαίνω), [in LXX: Psa.101:3 (שֵׂט), 4Ki.2:24 A, Wis.14:31, 2Ma.15:10 * ;]
1. a going aside, a deviation (Arist.).
2. In later writers, an overstepping; metaphorically, transgression (Plut., al.) : Rom.4:15 5:14, Heb.2:2 9:15; τ. νόμου, Rom.2:23; ἐν π., 1Ti.2:14; τ. παραβάσεων χάριν, Gal.3:19
SYN.: see: ἁμαρτία (AS)

elsewhere.note: You who glory in the law, do you dishonor God by disobeying the law?
Then why is there the law? It was added because of transgressions, until the offspring should come to whom the promise has been made. It was ordained through…
Adam wasn’t deceived, but the woman, being deceived, has fallen into disobedience;
For if the word spoken through angels proved steadfast, and every transgression and disobedience received a just penalty,
